lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Why does a bucket of cinema popcorn cost ten dollars?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The surprising answer has almost nothing to do with the corn.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everyone in the queue pays the ten dollars, because the film is about to start.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most of us assume the cinema makes its money from our *tickets*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the US and Canada, the average ticket in 2025 cost about eleven dollars and thirty cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your ticket goes to the cinema, and about half of that money goes on to the studio.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Of every ticket dollar last year, the world's biggest cinema chain paid studios about forty eight cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The studio's cut can be *seventy* percent in the opening week, and about thirty five by week six.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most tickets sell in those first weeks, when the cinema may keep just thirty cents of each dollar.
